t: How Many Copies Has GTA 6 Sold? 32.5 Million Before Launch
r: Official figures: GTA 6 sold 32.5 million copies before release and made $3.79 billion in day one retail sales, according to Take-Two.

l: GTA 6 sold 32.5 million copies before release and made $3.79 billion in day one retail sales. These are official figures from the Rockstar and Take-Two announcement on November 20.
Metric · Take-Two announcement
Copies sold before release · 32.5 million
Day one retail sales · $3.79 billion

The company notes that the dollar figure is its own estimate through the end of November 19, worldwide, and calls it the biggest entertainment launch in history. A copy count including sales since launch isn't out yet.
Before the announcement, this page carried a Sensor Tower estimate that turned out well below the official figure. It stays below only for the PS5 and Xbox split, which Take-Two hasn't shared.
Metric · Sensor Tower estimate
Copies sold, all platforms · 24.58 million
Revenue · About $2.36 billion
PS5 share · 75% of copies
Xbox Series X/S share · 25% of copies

If that 75/25 split holds for the whole total, it works out to around 18.4 million copies on PS5 and 6.1 million on Xbox. That math is ours, based on the figures above, not something Sensor Tower published.

Sensor Tower tracks how releases perform across the games industry and keeps a live database of what each one earns. GamesRadar+ pulled the figures from that tool and notes that the bulk of the revenue most likely came from pre-orders.
Analyst estimates can shift and can be off. They give a sense of how big the launch was, but the number that counts is the official one at the top of this page.

p.h: Why PS5 is so far ahead
l: GamesRadar+ says the gap was expected well before release:
there are simply far more PS5 consoles out there than Xbox Series machines;
Sony partnered with Rockstar and leaned hard into marketing;
GTA 6 was the PS5's startup graphic for a while, and it came back for launch.
For how the game actually runs on each console, see GTA 6 FPS and performance on PS5 Pro and Xbox.
PC isn't part of the count because GTA 6 hasn't come out on PC, and GamesRadar+ points out that Rockstar hasn't even confirmed that version yet. More in is GTA 6 on PC, PS4 or Xbox One.

p.h: Still deciding which edition to buy?
l: What each edition includes is covered in GTA 6 Ultimate Edition bonuses.
How many copies has GTA 6 sold? It sold 32.5 million copies before release alone, according to Take-Two's official announcement. A total including sales since launch hasn't been published.
How much money has GTA 6 made? Take-Two announced $3.79 billion in day one retail sales, based on company estimates through the end of November 19.
Did GTA 6 sell more on PS5 or Xbox? PS5, by a wide margin. Sensor Tower estimates a 75% share for PS5 and 25% for Xbox Series X|S.
Jason and Lucia in an official GTA 6 image released by Rockstar Games.

t: GTA 6 UFO House Easter Egg: Where the San Andreas House Is and How to Get In
r: The UFO house Rockstar teased in the San Andreas remaster is in GTA 6, in Bellville, Leonard County. The front door is fake, but you can break in through the garage.

l: The UFO house is in GTA 6. Back in 2021, Rockstar slipped an image of a house with a flying saucer over it into the GTA San Andreas remaster, and fans bet it was a hint at the next game. ZacCoxTV found that same house in Bellville, Leonard County, and Milo got inside too, holding it up against the 2021 image. InkTV is the third channel to show the place inside and out. The front door is fake, but the garage opens, and whoever lives there is deep into conspiracy theories.
Region: Leonard County, north of Vice City. InkTV puts it in the southern part of Leonard County, just above Vice-Dale County.
Town: Bellville, a small neighborhood of houses with white picket fences.
The house: yellow, with a double garage and a for-sale sign in the yard. There's usually a car parked out front.
The map is huge, so ZacCoxTV recommends flying in by helicopter. From the air you can also spot a rude joke a neighbor mowed into his lawn.
Head to the house in Bellville.
The front door and windows don't open. Go to the garage.
Get close and the game shows a break in prompt. Break into the garage and walk in.
Breaking in calls the cops. ZacCoxTV got a wanted level right away and was busted on his first try. There's also a dog in the yard and a snake in the garage that attacked him. Save before you go.
Milo found one more scare: pop the trunk of the car parked at the house and a huge snake comes out. That was all he found in there.
InkTV opened the same trunk and got something else entirely: an H&L .38 revolver and nothing more. So the trunk contents seem to change between playthroughs. Either way, open it carefully.
The garage is a paranoid neighbor's hideout:
Conspiracy boards: clippings about a woman who walks through walls, "America's most abducted man" and the Skunk Ape. Milo also found a newspaper story about that woman.

A Skunk Ape magazine: Milo found it lying on the bed. The cover InkTV shows has the Skunk Ape standing on top of pyramids, with more mystery stories inside. It's about the creature that has its own mission in the game (see the Skunk Ape mission).
More boards: InkTV also points out a drawing of a UFO lifting a car and the all-seeing eye symbol that GTA V players will recognize.
Radio and food: a radio and snacks you can pick up, including a meteorite-themed candy bar.
A piece of meteorite: you can grab it and sell it. In the game, a buyer on the Lifeinvader marketplace says they'll pay for what you find.
A collectible card: a card from The Legends of Ratface set, which counts toward the game's card collection.

ZacCoxTV didn't find anything else on his first visit. The clippings could be hinting at other secrets, but so far nobody has shown an actual UFO connection. Another UFO hunter's hideout sits in the watchtower shed on Mount Kalaga, behind a keypad; see the easter eggs list. For an actual flying saucer, see the UFO abduction in Kelly County.

p.h: The owner worked out they’re in a game
l: PC Gamer walked into the garage by day and found a huge board with "IT'S A SIMULATION" in red. The notes ask why the owner can't leave Leonida, count 140 identical people and puzzle over the number 6 and who "L" and "J" are. Boat brochures lie around, so the joke is that they plan to sail for the edge of the map.
The UFO house image showed up in the San Andreas remaster in 2021. Finding that exact house in GTA 6, covered in abduction clippings, is Rockstar landing the joke five years later.
More secrets in the GTA 6 easter eggs list.
Where is the UFO house in GTA 6? In Bellville, a small town in Leonard County north of Vice City. It's a yellow house with a double garage and a for-sale sign.
Can you go inside the GTA 6 UFO house? Not through the front door. ZacCoxTV got in by breaking into the garage, where the owner keeps a conspiracy hideout.
What's inside the UFO house? A conspiracy den: corkboards full of clippings, a Skunk Ape magazine, a radio, snacks and a collectible card.
What's in the trunk of the car at the UFO house? It varies. Milo got a huge snake, while InkTV found an H&L .38 revolver. Open it carefully and be ready to back off.
The yellow house with the double garage and for-sale sign, in Bellville.
InkTV found an H&L .38 revolver in the trunk of the car parked outside the house.

t: GTA 6 Collectible Cards: Locations and How Much They Sell For
r: GTA 6 collectible cards hide in safes and stashes and sell at pawn shops. The one in the early warehouse fetches $6,000 in Hamlet. Here are the confirmed locations and whether you should sell.

l: GTA 6 collectible cards are tucked away in safes and stashes around the map, and you can sell them at a pawn shop. The easiest one sits in a warehouse safe near Jason's house and goes for about $6,000 at Hamlet Pawn. A full card map hasn't been published yet.
Card · Where · Shown by

Leroy Rook (Silver), from the Vice City Narcos set · Office safe in the abandoned warehouse south of Vice-Dale County, near Jason's house · DooDooPoo, GrandTheftIntel, Musty Sky, Arekkz Gaming, FuriousFade, Rodwenn and BennyCentral
The Legends of Ratface · Hidden stash in the garage of the UFO house in Bellville, Leonard County · ZacCoxTV
Two cards · The Key Lento radio tower, about 0.36 miles from Jason's house: one in the room near the top, one inside the phone box · Millzaa, Arekkz Gaming, Rodwenn and BennyCentral
Trailer safe card · A trailer on the west side of a small trailer park in the swamp west of the Keys · RageGamingVideos
Cards on a garage table · The garage of a mansion on Vespucci Island, Vice City, the same island as Paul Walker's car · Imack Studios

The warehouse safe has no code: spin the right stick until the lock gives. You can get there right after the prologue. Its card is Leroy Rook (Silver): FuriousFade read the name out as he opened the safe, and Arekkz's screen shows a "Vice City Narcos 1/24" counter.

Climb the tower using the stairs inside and the ladders outside. In the room near the top there's a card on a table next to a magazine. Millzaa pulled Thelma, who he says is one of 18 Delights dancers. A second card sits inside the phone box out on the balcony: his came from the backyard wrestling set, which he says has 12. Rodwenn warns that the top card isn't worth much, and Millzaa confirms it: $20 at the Hamlet pawn shop. The same climb has a sniper and a parachute; see GTA 6 secret early items.

According to RageGamingVideos, in the swamp west of the Keys, where the game starts, there's a small trailer park next to a story mission marker. The trailer on its west side has a safe, and the code is on the photos inside the trailer, which you can zoom in on. The card inside sold for $1,350 at a pawn shop. It's on the way to the Kingfishers' fishing shacks.

Imack Studios opened the garage of a mansion full of expensive cars on Vespucci Island (press Triangle, or Y on Xbox, and play the lock minigame). Inside, there are collectible cards on a table to grab and sell.

p.h: Found, but no exact spot yet
l: Sports card in an RV: WiLLiSGaming says some RVs out in the wilderness have a lockbox, and the code is usually written on the wall. One of them held a collectible sports card. The spot is only shown on the map in his video. The swamp trailer RageGamingVideos showed above works the same way.
Other sets: T5G found cards from an X-Men parody, dancers from the 919 Club and American wrestlers. He didn't give locations.
Everything else is not mapped yet. We'll add locations here as they get confirmed.

p.h: Where to sell and what they’re worth
l: Head to a pawn shop. The first one is in Hamlet, marked with a green icon on the map, per Musty Sky.
Talk to the clerk and pick the option to sell collectibles. DooDooPoo pressed Y on Xbox.
The menu has two tabs: Collectible Cards and Collectible Items.
Pick a set and use Sell All to sell every card you have from it.

The warehouse card went for $6,000 in videos from DooDooPoo, GrandTheftIntel and Musty Sky. This page used to say no one had posted prices for the others. Now there are two: the swamp trailer card sold for $1,350 (RageGamingVideos), and the table card on the radio tower is worth just $20 (Millzaa). RaidAway took two cards to a pawn shop: a backyard wrestling card was worth $150, and a comic card $50. Prices vary a lot.

Check the value before you go. Millzaa shows you can see what your cards are worth straight from the map: hover over the Hamlet pawn shop. In Rodwenn's video, the shop's map card lists $6,000 in collectibles to sell while he's carrying the warehouse card. The same card says the shop buys cards, doubloons and meteorites.

In DooDooPoo's video, the Collectible Cards list has 18 rows, and only Vice City Narcos was unlocked. The rest show as Undiscovered. T5G says the cards you collect get stored in a box in Jason's house. GamesRadar+ notes that the Exploration tab of the map index lists pawn shop collectors.
There's a case for both:
Sell: the Pixel Art cheat asks you to make $250,000 selling collectibles. And $6,000 early in the game goes a long way, as Musty Sky points out.
Keep: the Don't Touch My Deck trophy wants 3 complete card sets. The Bubblegum cheat asks you to find all 24 cards in the Vice City Flamingos set.

No source has tested whether a sold card still counts toward its set. If the trophy matters to you, hold on to your cards until that's cleared up. Cheats only work after you finish the story; see the full cheat list.
The total hasn't been revealed. Here's what is known:
The Vice City Flamingos set has 24 cards, per PC Gamer and GamesRadar+.
The Vice City Narcos set, home of the warehouse card, also has 24: the "1/24" counter shows on Arekkz Gaming's screen.
According to Millzaa, the Delights dancers set has 18 cards and the backyard wrestling set has 12.
The trophy asks for 3 complete sets, so there are at least three.
The pawn shop list shows 18 rows in DooDooPoo's video, but nobody has confirmed that each row is a set.
Where do you sell collectible cards in GTA 6? At a pawn shop. Hamlet Pawn, near Jason's house, paid $6,000 for the warehouse card in videos from DooDooPoo, GrandTheftIntel and Musty Sky.

How many collectible cards are in GTA 6? Nobody has published the total. Vice City Flamingos and Vice City Narcos have 24 cards each. According to Millzaa, the Delights dancers set has 18 and the backyard wrestling set has 12.
Should I sell collectible cards in GTA 6? Selling gets you quick cash, but there's a trophy for completing 3 sets. Nobody has tested yet whether a sold card still counts toward its set.
Where is the early game collectible card? In the office safe of an abandoned warehouse south of Vice-Dale County, a short drive from Jason's house. Spin the right stick to open it.
The Hamlet Pawn menu on the Collectible Cards tab, with a Vice City Narcos card ready to sell.

t: GTA 6: Where to Find Your First Plane and Helicopter (Near Jason's House)
r: In GTA 6, seaplanes and a helicopter sit unguarded in Southwind, about 2.5 miles from Jason's house in Key Lento. You can take them without getting a wanted level.

l: You can fly almost from the start of GTA 6. Near Jason's house, in Southwind, there are seaplanes and a helicopter nobody is guarding. According to PC Gamer, you can take them without getting a single star. Nerpah showed the same spot and has a good tip: grab one early and use it to explore the map and reach the rare cars faster.
From Jason's house in Key Lento, drive about 2.5 miles southwest:
Stay on Sunbelt Highway (Route 1) the whole way.
Go southwest through Key Lento, then west through Abismo Key.
You'll cross two long bridges. After them the highway bends north and you enter Southwind.
On your right there's a concrete barrier along the road. Where it ends, turn right into the parking lot at the sign for SBW (Sherwin Boatworks) and Chicki's Tiki Bar.
Southwind is right next to the military base, Mile Zero Air Station.
Facing the water (east), on your right (south) there's a small hangar with a few Mammoth Dodo seaplanes in and around it, and sometimes a couple more moored off the dock.
They're not the fastest planes, but they land on water and on land and need very little room to take off. Perfect for exploring.
Drive one into the water and take off, or grab one from the dock.
From the parking lot entrance, look straight east. An open gate leads to a dock with a Buckingham Maverick. Ignore the no-trespassing sign, run to the dock and hop in.
A commercial jet: the GTA 6 airport.
A fighter jet or a tank: the military base.
Before you fly, grab a parachute.
Where is the closest plane to Jason's house in GTA 6? In Southwind, in a small hangar next to the Sherwin Boatworks and Chicki's Tiki Bar parking lot. Mammoth Dodo seaplanes are parked there.
Where can you find a helicopter early in GTA 6? In the same spot in Southwind: a Buckingham Maverick sits on the dock east of the parking lot.
Do you get a wanted level for taking these planes? No. According to PC Gamer there's never anyone around, so you can take them without drawing attention.
The Leonida Keys, where Jason's house is, in an official image.

t: GTA 6 Bigfoot (Skunk Ape) Mission: How to Start It and Get the Camo Sniper Rifle
r: GTA 6's Bigfoot is the start of a hidden side quest. After you black out at the effigy in Grassrivers, find a note, call the number and hunt the Skunk Ape at night. The reward is a unique camo sniper rifle.

l: GTA 6's "Bigfoot" isn't just a jump scare: it's the start of a hidden side quest. The creature is called the Skunk Ape (the characters call it Mr. Mangrove), it lives in the Grassrivers swamps, and hunting it down gets you a unique, fully camouflaged sniper rifle. JFM showed the quest from start to finish. T5G, ZacCoxTV and Punish also ran into the Skunk Ape or its effigy, The Easter Egg Hunter showed the start of the hunt with Kirk, and PC Gamer wrote up an easy route to the first sighting.
The catch: the game doesn't tell you what to do after the first encounter. Lots of players stop at the scare and never find the quest.

Drive the roads of Grassrivers. On one stretch the Skunk Ape shows up eating a deer in the middle of the road. ZacCoxTV and T5G saw this too, and T5G spotted signs around the map warning that the Skunk Ape is in the area.
It runs into the woods. Follow it into the trees.
You'll find an effigy, a human-shaped figure made of wood and vines.
Examine it. Jason blacks out and, for a moment, you see the Skunk Ape up close.

p.h: Another way in: PC Gamer’s boat route
l: PC Gamer describes a route that starts at home, by boat:
Start at Jason's first house and take his boat from the dock out back.
Cross Gambit Bay and head for the dead-end road on the inner side of the peninsula across the water.
Before you even reach land, a prompt tells you to switch on Focus mode and track down where the noises are coming from.
The Skunk Ape bolts into the mangroves. Keep using Focus to chase it. You'll lose sight of it and find the effigy next to a tree instead.

PC Gamer says the creature gives off a green cloud of stink, and that smell is what knocks Jason out when he checks the effigy, right after a close look at its huge feet. PC Gamer doesn't name the region for this spot, so it isn't clear whether it's the same stretch of swamp as the deer encounter above.

p.h: Step 2: the note and the phone call
l: This is the part everyone misses. According to JFM, nearby there's a note stuck on a wall next to an ATM, asking you to call a number.

PC Gamer describes the lead a little differently: after the sighting, look for Skunk Ape flyers on storefronts and telephone poles around Leonida, which point you to the quest. It may well be the same notice in more than one place, but nobody has compared the two yet.
Find the note and read it.
Call the number on your in-game phone.
The man who answers is Kirk, a Skunk Ape hunter. He marks a spot labeled KK on your map, in the swamp.
In The Easter Egg Hunter's video, the call goes to voicemail. In the message, Kirk says he's out chasing the Skunk Ape and can be found in Pelican Valley most evenings.
Go to the KK spot at night. According to JFM, the quest won't continue during the day. Kirk's voicemail fits that, since he says he's out there most evenings.
Kirk checks your "readings" and decides you've seen Mr. Mangrove. In The Easter Egg Hunter's video he flies drones, checks Jason's EMF and says he still has the creature's spores on him.
To prove his point, Kirk has you grab a stick and hit his truck hard (The Easter Egg Hunter).
During the hunt, follow the drone's light. And keep your gun away: Kirk says a bullet could make the creature release a toxic cloud, and he wants it alive.
Chase the creature through the woods, following its roars. You'll pass its camps, bones and more effigies.
At one point something huge comes after you and you have to run back to the truck. Jason may black out again but doesn't die, and the quest continues.
A large area is then marked in pink on the map. Inside it there are three effigies to find.
JFM's tip: grab a boat and cruise the area with Focus mode on. The effigies light up in Focus. It takes about 10 minutes.

p.h: Step 5: the helicopter and the ending
l: You hunt the Skunk Ape from a helicopter, already holding your new sniper rifle.
After you hit it, find it knocked out in one of the back rooms of the area.
Then things get weird: you turn into a frog and then a fly, and overhear Kirk planning to cut you out of the money.
In the end, you choose whether to help Kirk or let the Skunk Ape get him. JFM let the creature take Kirk.
The quest ends with the camo sniper rifle in your arsenal.
Whether the final choice changes the reward.
The exact spot of the note on the map. JFM shows it in his video from 1:38.

The start of the quest (Kirk's voicemail and the night hunt) also shows up in The Easter Egg Hunter's video. The whole quest, all the way to the rifle, has only been shown by JFM so far, so the badge still says "Unverified". More secrets in the GTA 6 easter eggs list.
Is there Bigfoot in GTA 6? Yes. It's called the Skunk Ape, Florida's version of Bigfoot, and it lives in the Grassrivers swamps. Players have seen it eating a deer on the road.

How do you start the Bigfoot mission in GTA 6? Find the Skunk Ape on the road in Grassrivers, follow it into the trees and examine the effigy. After Jason blacks out, find the note with a phone number and call it.
What do you get from the Skunk Ape mission in GTA 6? A unique, fully camouflaged and very powerful sniper rifle that you keep at the end.
Who is Mr. Mangrove in GTA 6? It's the name the quest characters give the Skunk Ape, the hairy creature of the Grassrivers swamps.
The wooden effigy in the Grassrivers swamp. Examine it and Jason blacks out.
Grassrivers, the swamps where the Skunk Ape lives, in an official image.

t: GTA 6 Bank Account and ATMs: How to Deposit and Protect Your Cash
r: Your GTA 6 bank account unlocks in the Chapter 1 mission Buck Me, and then any ATM takes deposits. Until then, hide your cash under the bedroom floorboards in Key Lento.

l: Your GTA 6 bank account unlocks in Chapter 1, during the mission Buck Me. From then on you can deposit cash at any ATM on the map. Before that, the safe place for money is the stash at home.

According to Hazard, Buck Me shows up after the party Jason and his friends throw for Lucia at the Rusty Anchor, a couple of hours into the game at most. In it you open a checking account and make your first deposit at an ATM.
Early on, a few hundred dollars can make or break you, and the money in your wallet is never fully safe:
Dying or getting arrested costs you. PC Gamer puts the penalty at a few hundred dollars. MrBossFTW and Vice City Dispatch describe something harsher: you drop all the loose cash you were carrying.

Strangers on the street may try to rob you. Milo tested the rumor that locals mug people at ATMs and got held up outside a store with no ATM at all. It isn't just a bank thing, so don't carry more than you need.
There's a cap: you can only carry up to $20,000 on you. Mr Lawrence and Vice City Dispatch give the same number, so once you get close, go deposit.
So the habit to build is simple: stash often.

p.h: Before the bank: the floorboard stash
l: For the first few chapters you have no account. You can still hide money under the floorboards in the bedroom of Jason's house in Key Lento. Whatever sits there stays put if you die or get busted.
More on that in do you lose money when you die.

Hazard describes the stash as a hole under the floorboard with a lockbox and a pile of cash. He also flags a catch at this stage: without an account, you can't pay for repairs at a gas station or Pay 'n' Spray, because they only take BuckMe. Cash still works at grocery stores and for fuel. Other channels show gas station repairs without mentioning this, so treat it as his experience.

p.h: Stolen goods go in the trunk
l: Jewelry, drugs and marked bills from robberies can sit in your car's trunk. Even if the cops impound the car, you can get the haul back later and sell it.
Just don't use a car you don't own. Lose the car and you lose what's inside. When it's time to sell, see the fence locations.

p.h: How to deposit at an ATM
l: Play up to the mission Buck Me in Chapter 1. It opens your account.

On the map, look for the hand with a credit card icon. Those are ATMs. According to BennyCentral, the BuckMe app on your phone points you to the nearest one. Deposits only happen at an ATM, not from your phone.
Walk up to one and interact with it.
Choose to deposit.

p.h: What the ATM screen looks like
l: Mr Lawrence recorded a deposit with no commentary at all, so everything here comes from what's on screen. Hover over the icon on the map and its label reads ATM; you can set it as your destination from there. He used one in Key Lento, mounted on the wall of a green wooden building.
The screen is called Your Account, with your balance in the top right corner.
There are three options: Deposit, Withdraw and Transactions, plus Exit. With a $0 balance in his video, Withdraw was grayed out.
PS5 buttons: Cross selects, Circle backs out and R2 zooms in on the screen.
Two balances on your HUD: the top one, next to a small "b" logo, is your BuckMe account; the one underneath is the cash in your pocket. It's a quick way to check the deposit went through.
Having an account also unlocks some weapons for purchase. PC Gamer mentions an interest-bearing savings account too, but doesn't explain how it works.
MrBossFTW explains what changes once the story opens your BuckMe account:
the money in it can be used by both Jason and Lucia;
it isn't lost when you die or get arrested;
there's a deposit limit, and it goes up as you progress through the main story.
His routine: early on, keep most of your money in the safehouse stash. Once the account opens, grab the stash and deposit it into BuckMe.

Your account has a deposit cap. Near the end of Chapter 1, Elanip got an "Account Limit $15,000" notice on the ATM screen. Soon after, the account was full and the ATM wouldn't take any more, leaving him holding the cash while the cops closed in.
MrBossFTW says the cap rises with the story. Hazard explains it differently: BuckMe perks grow as you save money. By his account:
How much you save · Account limit · Extra perk
$10,000 · $100,000 · 20% off RideMe trips
$100,000 or more · $500,000 · 20% off garage purchases
That table comes from Hazard's voiceover alone; the app screen isn't shown in his video. Still, the first tier matches the "Account Limit $15,000" Elanip saw. See garage locations and prices.

p.h: The couple’s savings and the ending
l: Heads up: this part covers how the ending is decided, without giving away the story.

According to GameSpot, Jason and Lucia's shared savings max out at $2 million. Hitting that cap while their relationship is also maxed out is what earns the best ending. A maxed relationship without full savings gets you a good ending, but not the best one. The details are in how many endings GTA 6 has.
In other words, what you save isn't just protection against losing cash. It counts toward the end of the game.
Channels don't agree yet on how much the story asks you to save:
$5,000: WiLLiSGaming says that early on Jason's credit is too bad for a normal bank account, so the bank gives you the BuckMe app instead and asks you to build up $5,000 before the story moves on.

A goal per chapter: Vice City Dispatch, which builds its videos from review excerpts, says BuckMe sets a savings target each chapter and rewards you for hitting it. One review it quotes describes a family savings account with targets starting at $100,000, then $500,000, and says those deposits can't be withdrawn.

Both could be true, with the bigger numbers coming in later chapters, but no video has shown those larger goals on screen yet. Note that Vice City Dispatch's $100,000 and $500,000 are the same figures Hazard gives as account limits, not goals. And GameSpot puts the cap on the couple's savings at $2 million. For now, follow whatever goal your game gives you. Also note the regular ATM does have a Withdraw option, so if that lock exists, it applies to the family savings goal, not your everyday account.
This is the guide's key advice. Plenty of GTA 6's street moments only happen if you have cash in hand:
a stranger selling secrets, each one pricier than the last;
a bribe to get quick access to a restricted area;
a pool hustler in a dive bar;
vendors who only take cash.
So whenever you deposit, keep a few hundred in your wallet. That way you won't have to run off looking for an ATM in the middle of one of those encounters.
To fill the account up, see how to make money in GTA 6.
How do you open a bank account in GTA 6? It unlocks during the Chapter 1 mission Buck Me. After that, ATMs accept deposits.
Where are the ATMs in GTA 6? Look for the icon of a hand holding a credit card on the map. Walk up to the machine and interact with it to deposit.
How much cash can you carry in GTA 6? Up to $20,000 on your person, according to PC Gamer, Mr Lawrence and Vice City Dispatch. Anything beyond that should go into your stash or the bank.
Should you deposit all your money in GTA 6? No. Keep a few hundred dollars in your wallet for bribes, pool games, cash-only vendors and other street encounters.
The ATM screen: deposit, withdraw or check your account transactions.

t: GTA 6 Parrot Money: How to Rob the "Strange Noises" Liquor Store
r: The Three Sheets liquor store hides over $2,000 in its Exotic Animals Front ("Strange Noises") operation: a safe, the register and a stash only the parrot gives away, in the vent by the generator.

l: The parrot money is at the Three Sheets liquor store, the same one where Jason's neighbor Shirley sends you to pick up rum. The back room runs an exotic animal smuggling racket with over $2,000 lying around, and the best part sits in a stash only the parrot gives away. Five channels showed the same robbery: TheProfessional, vassillios16, Arekkz Gaming, KultZ and KhrazeGaming. GamesRadar+ has since published a full guide and gives the official name: in game it's the Exotic Animals Front illegal operation. The store is in Key Lento, just north of the Pay 'n' Spray there.

Go to the liquor store. If you took Shirley's side job, this is where you pick up her bottle. According to GamesRadar+, Shirley lives a few doors down from Jason, in the house with the orange and green parasol, and she wants a bottle of Salty Squid rum.
Inside, you'll hear animal noises from the back. The clerk claims it's the animal channel on TV.
When you leave the store, the spot appears on your map as a robbery called "Strange Noises": the clerk seems distracted by something in the back.
If you're carrying Shirley's rum, GamesRadar+ suggests stowing it in your trunk before you head round the back.

On the way: before you leave for the store, give Shirley's dog Argula a pet. GamesRadar+ says it counts as a thoughtful action and can raise your focus bar, depending on your criminal profile. See how to pet animals.
You don't need Shirley's job for this. vassillios16 went straight there after the prologue. If you can't see the store, look up liquor stores in the map index.
Park in the alley next to the store.
Climb the dumpster (or hop the chain-link gate) into the back area. GamesRadar+ climbed the fence on the left side of the store as you face it.
About four guys are waiting. They grab machetes, and one may pull a gun.
TheProfessional recommends knocking them all out with your fists. Gunfire brings the cops; without them you can loot at your own pace.
How many guards? This page said "about four", going by the videos. GamesRadar+ counts five or six armed criminals patrolling the walled-off area, so plan for the bigger number.
GamesRadar+ suggests a stealthy approach that counts toward a professional criminal profile:
Pick up the bottles scattered around the area.
Throw them to make noise and lure the guards out of the walled section one at a time.
Take each one down quietly.
Going in guns blazing works too, but it pushes your profile toward violent and brings the cops. More on that in GTA 6 criminal profile explained.
Where · How much
Stash behind the generator · About $1,300 to $1,400
Back room safe · About $900
Cash counting machine · About $200
Register up front · About $200
The thugs' pockets · Small change
The safe has no code: rotate the right stick until the lock gives, like the other early safes.
There's a parrot in the back that keeps squawking about "cash" and a "stash".
Walk up to the cage and press LT (L2 on PS5) to talk to it.
Ask where the money is. In GamesRadar+'s guide the options are "Cash?" and then "Where's the cash?". It repeats "generator, generator".
Walk to the generator but don't touch it. Open the grate right behind it.
The cash is inside.
Facing the parrot, the generator is straight ahead and to the left, in the corner. Next to it is a white vent you can open. GamesRadar+ found exactly $1,263 in it.

Arekkz Gaming describes the same spot: the generator is in the back left corner and the stash is a vent in the wall, worth about $1,200. KultZ pulled about $1,300 from the vent. vassillios16 found the stash without talking to the parrot, since it sits in a corner of the back area. If you can't spot it, ask the bird. You can even thank it on the way out.

Check the cages. If the cops aren't right on top of you, GamesRadar+ reminds you to study the birds in the cages to add them to your animal collection. The door nearby leads to the safe and the money counter, with one more guard to deal with.
KhrazeGaming points out this exotic animal front is easy to miss if you never check the back. He also says enemy hideouts like this one refresh every few in-game days and restock.

Expect the cops. Both creators escaped by car without much trouble. Take the cash home, because dying wipes your wallet. For more early robberies, see how to make money in GTA 6 and the early money warehouse.

Where is the parrot money in GTA 6? At the Three Sheets liquor store, the same one Shirley sends you to for rum. The parrot in the back keeps saying "generator": the cash is behind the grate right behind the generator.

What is the Strange Noises robbery in GTA 6? It's the robbery that shows up on your map after you hear animal noises in the liquor store's back room and the clerk plays it off. The back hides an exotic animal smuggling ring and cash.
How much money is in the parrot stash? Over $2,000 in total: about $1,300 in the stash ($1,263 in GamesRadar+'s guide), about $900 in the safe and a bit more in the cash counter and the register.
How do you talk to the parrot in GTA 6? Once the guards are down, walk up to the cage, press LT (L2 on PS5) and pick "Cash?" and then "Where's the cash?". It tells you the money is by the generator.
The liquor store's back room: a front for smuggling exotic animals.

t: How to Make Money Fast in GTA 6: Best Early and Late Game Methods
r: The fastest ways to make money in GTA 6: Kenton's shipwreck dives (up to $4,000), Dog Island, Donnie's packages, robbing other criminals, selling stolen cars and the Ambrosia demolition derby.

l: Money is tight at the start of GTA 6, and there's no shortcut: the $250,000 money cheat only works after you beat the story. Until then, these are the methods players have shown working, with how much each one paid. For a route of early stashes packed with cash and guns, see GTA 6 secret early items.

WiLLiSGaming, who already got past chapter 2, warns that your cash goes back to zero when chapter 2 starts. The only money that carries over is the family savings: the $5,000 the story asks you to put into the BuckMe app (Jason has bad credit, so the bank gives him the app to build it). So in chapter 1, get the $5,000 and keep the story moving. Don't spend hours grinding.
Method · Payout shown · Source
Pilot Pete's drops (chapter 4) · $10,000 to $20,000 · PC Gamer
Robbing a store through the back (chapter 3) · $6,000 to $15,000 · PC Gamer
Selling stolen cars (chapter 2 on) · $1,000 to $20,000 · PC Gamer
Robbing other criminals mid-escape · $1,000 to $15,000 · PC Gamer
Demolition derby at Ambrosia Raceway · $3,800 to $6,300 per win · PC Gamer
A rare trading card at a pawn shop · $6,000 · LoDj1c
Red warehouse bag sold at Donnie's · about $10,000 ($800 more than at Brian's) · BennyCentral
Kenton's shipwreck dives · up to $4,000 per dive · WiLLiSGaming, JoblessGarrett
Gellhorn Raceway (win) · up to $4,000, minus about $500 to rent a car · MrRoflWaffles
Southside trap house · over $3,000, plus a rifle · BennyCentral
King Fishers island raid · about $2,000 · KultZ
Dog Island · $1,218 · ZoneX
Store register holdup (early game) · almost $600 to just over $1,000 · KultZ, KhrazeGaming
Brian's Lab Fees rent job · $600, one time only · KultZ
Money cheat (after the story) · $250,000 · GamesRadar+, PC Gamer

Kenton, a scuba instructor, texts you shipwreck locations. Dive with his gear and a metal detector, collect the treasure and sell it back to him. Up to $4,000 per dive, and he pays more the more you do. Full guide: GTA 6 sunken treasure.
Swim with no boat in the middle of Gambit Bay until a dog on a jet ski rescues you. On its island, a dog digs up about $1,200. See the jet ski dog.

p.h: Donnie’s lost packages and Brian’s lockup
l: Donnie loses packages that show up on your map. Pick them up and bring them to Donnie's trailer: according to WiLLiSGaming he pays more than Brian. Use Focus mode, because the packages have a tracker that makes a sound Focus can show you. Anything else illegal you find can be sold at Brian's lockup (enter the code on the keypad and drop it in his strongbox).

Check the mailbox at Jason's house after main missions. There's often cash waiting, usually with a text from Donnie letting you know. ImBones points out that rewards from main missions and side quests both land there, so if you never check it, the money just sits.

KultZ lays out an easy first payday: after the mission Gone Fishing, do Lab Fees, the job listed as collecting Brian's rent. Drop the bag in the container at Brian's lockup in South Key Lento. Your wallet stays empty at first; give it a little while, then check the mailbox in front of the house for the $600. He notes this job only pays out once.

Some RVs out in the wild have lockboxes, and the code is usually written on the wall. WiLLiSGaming says they almost always have good loot, like a rare sports trading card. Cards sell at pawn shops: LoDj1c got $6,000 for one at the Hamlet pawn shop. He found that card in a safe inside a building in South Vice-Dale County, near Jason's place, along with cash and cargo worth about $10,000 in total.

DPJ showed the same kind of warehouse in South Vice-Dale County, near Hamlet, with everyone inside already dead: no fight needed. He found a bag with $4,800, drugs in the back of a truck, a Duke 5.56 assault rifle and the safe with the card (rotate the right stick to open it). Bring a car: your bags fill up fast and you can stash the rest in the trunk. The cash comes as marked bills, which you have to take to a fence. GrandTheftIntel hit the same warehouse and walked out with around $11,000 plus a card worth $6,000. Full walkthrough: the early money warehouse.

BennyCentral showed the same red warehouse and a way to squeeze more out of it: compare your fences on the map before you sell. Donnie's trailer was paying $800 more than Brian's lockup for the exact same bag, which came to about $10,000, plus the loose cash you grab on the way. The payment arrives in the mailbox outside your house.
BennyCentral rates this a medium security job and a quick earner. It's in Southside, Vice City, where the PTT Youngs gang grows weed and stashes stolen goods.
Clear the yard first, then head inside.
There's cash on the desk by the money counter, weed on the kitchen counter and in the grow room, pills in the bedroom and jewelry on a table.
Don't leave without the luxury watch next to the kitchen sink.
An assault rifle is lying on the bedroom floor.

He made over $3,000 in a couple of minutes. Benny doesn't say whether it needs the Ultimate Edition; that edition has a similar bonus, the PTT Youngin$ Compound, also in Southside. See Ultimate Edition bonuses.

According to BennyCentral, hovering over a robbery spot on the map brings up a card with its security level and take value. A high security warehouse, for example, pays up to $6,400. Start with the low security ones and work your way up, and use your binoculars to tag enemies from a distance before going in. JorRaptor adds that these illegal operations run on a cooldown: after a while you can rob them again, but for less loot than the first time, so hitting them early means they come back sooner. When you leave, check the icon on the map to see whether you got every valuable.

If doing the same robberies over and over gets old, MrRoflWaffles suggests racing at Gellhorn Raceway, which has its own icon on the map. Renting a car costs around $500, a win pays up to $4,000 and a race takes about five minutes. It's decent driving practice too.

Stop when something weird happens. RageGamingVideos saw an explosion off the coast east of Key Lento, found a shark attacking a man, killed it with the speargun from the scuba kit and picked up beeping packages from the water: about $2,000 worth of drugs to sell.

Milo explains what to watch for: if you're out on a boat and see another boat explode, a shark just hit it. Head for the wreckage, which is full of loot, but the shark is still around and will come for you. Get back on your boat, grab the speargun, take the shark out, and then collect everything to sell to Brian.
King Fishers gang bases are packed with contraband that sells well, and WiLLiSGaming found a unique rifle at one. Bring an empty bag and come prepared: he fought about 30 enemies.

KultZ did the payback job against the King Fishers on an island. To get there fast, steal a boat or seaplane; you'll usually find one near any stretch of water. Clear out the gang, pocket the loose cash and bag the rest, which is mostly drugs. Drop the haul at Brian's lockup and collect the money from your mailbox later. That one raid made him about $2,000, and he says another King Fishers job tends to pop up later, on your way to pick up Lucia.

You can rob convenience stores from the very start. KhrazeGaming got about $1,000 out of a register early on, and KultZ took almost $600 from one shop. KultZ likes going out late at night, when the streets are quieter and the stores are often empty. His take per night ranged from a few hundred dollars to more than $2,000 on his best nights. Wear sunglasses and a cap, and keep a spare outfit in your trunk to change into on the way out. For the safe in the back, see how to get safe codes, and to shake the cops afterward, how to lose the police.

p.h: The parrot behind the liquor store
l: Shirley's rum errand leads to a liquor store with something hidden out back. The full walkthrough is in the parrot money guide.

p.h: Later in the story (PC Gamer’s list)

l: BennyCentral warns against robbing banks and loan stores early on. The cash can come with dye packs, and the jammer that deals with them doesn't unlock until later in the story, so you risk losing the haul.

Listen for sirens, alarms, gunshots and screams. When you see a bank job, jewelry store heist or armored car robbery in progress, take down the crooks running off and grab their bags. Then get out fast, because their heat becomes yours. With Jason and Lucia together you can carry more bags.
All stolen goods (drugs, jewelry, marked bills) turn into cash at a fence. See GTA 6 fence locations.

In chapter 2 you meet Moses, a mechanic who buys older, low-profile cars and often tells you where the ones he wants are. In chapter 3, Randy pays more for flashy, expensive cars. See how to steal cars in GTA 6.

You win by default once every other car is wrecked, so you don't need to drive well. The oval pays over $3,800 and the figure-eight nearly double, up to $6,300. You can repeat it as often as you like and rent a car at the track for a few hundred dollars.
In chapter 2, Jason takes hunting jobs from his old army buddy Bret in Lummox County. He pays more for bigger animals, and there are legendary animals. PC Gamer got $2,500 for a big boar.

p.h: Rob stores through the back door
l: In chapter 3 you get a tool to pick locks. From then on, pick stores with a back door: sneak in, subdue the staff in the back, kill the alarm, destroy the security footage and find the safe before anyone notices. See how to get safe codes.

If you die or get busted with cash in your pocket, you lose it. Stash it at home. Once the bank unlocks in the chapter 1 mission Buck Me, MrDalekJD also stops at an ATM before every job, since money in your account is safe; you can only deposit at an ATM, not from your phone. See do you lose money when you die in GTA 6.

What is the fastest way to make money in GTA 6? Early on, Kenton's shipwreck dives and Dog Island. Later, according to PC Gamer, robbing other criminals mid-heist, selling stolen cars and the Ambrosia Raceway demolition derby, which pays up to $6,300 a win.
Does your money reset in GTA 6 chapter 2? According to WiLLiSGaming, yes: your cash goes back to zero when chapter 2 starts. Only the family savings, the $5,000 in the BuckMe app, carries over.
Is there a money cheat in GTA 6? Yes, it gives $250,000, but it only works after you beat the story.

Can you race for money in GTA 6? Yes. MrRoflWaffles races at Gellhorn Raceway, marked with an icon on the map: renting a car costs about $500, a win pays up to $4,000 and each race takes about five minutes.
Ambrosia, home of the raceway where the demolition derby pays the most, in an official image.

t: GTA 6 Beginner Tips: 15 Things to Know Before You Start
r: The best GTA 6 tips for beginners: settings worth changing, stashing your cash, the $5,000 BuckMe goal, your phone as a quest log, cops that remember you and more.

l: GTA 6 changes a lot compared with GTA 5, and some of those changes cost you if you don't know about them. Here are the beginner tips DPJ and WiLLiSGaming showed in gameplay, plus extra ones from MrDalekJD, KultZ, Arekkz Gaming and other channels.

Map on the View button. DPJ's trick: in Settings, set the View button to camera, zoom the camera all the way out, then set the button back to map. You keep the wider camera and the map is one press away.

Run by holding the stick. In the movement options, set running to holding the left stick forward and movement speed to "walk fast". It helps when you need to escape. BennyCentral likes a different speed, jog: a slight push on the stick walks, and pushing it all the way jogs, while clicking the left stick still sprints. It comes down to taste, so try both.
Drive-by aim assist on: aiming manually while driving is hard at first.
Sensitivity: if aiming feels sluggish, raise look sensitivity and aim acceleration a little (DPJ uses 9).
Vehicle camera: if it lags behind on turns, set the follow speed to around 5 or 6.

Stash your cash. If you die or get busted, you lose the money on you. Keep it under the floorboards at home and carry only what you'll spend. Once the bank unlocks through the story, MrDalekJD's habit is to stop at an ATM before anything risky. See do you lose money when you die and how the bank and ATMs work.

The $5,000 goal. Early on, Lucia wants a bank account but Jason has bad credit, so the bank gives him the BuckMe app. You need to save $5,000 in it before the story moves on, according to WiLLiSGaming.

Chapter 1 money resets. WiLLiSGaming warns that your cash goes back to zero when chapter 2 starts. Only the family savings in BuckMe stay. Don't grind a fortune in chapter 1. See how to make money fast.
Check the mailbox. After main missions there's often cash in the mailbox at Jason's house, usually with a text from Donnie.

Loot the bodies. MrDalekJD's advice: don't drive off the second a shootout ends. Downed enemies can drop cash, ammo and weapons, and when there are several of them it adds up fast, which matters early on when money and ammo are tight. Just remember that loose cash is only safe once you've stashed or banked it.

A lot is locked behind progress. Better cars, weapons, phone apps and faster money all depend on the story, DPJ says. You don't need to rush, but move on until you get the tools, like the slim jim and key cloner in how to steal cars. Other channels agree and give examples:
MrDalekJD: the bank and the slim jim both come through the story.
Arekkz Gaming: car customization, your bank account and the places where you sell valuables.
KhrazeGaming: key cloners, extra garages to register more cars and access to pricier places to break into. He says you'll have most of it by the middle of the story.

p.h: Your phone is your quest log
l: Pending jobs live on your phone. There's no reliable journal. Press Up on the D-pad: messages from characters list suggested jobs and past ones, and remind you of money waiting for you.

Apps worth knowing: Waink It (scans cars), Snapmatic (the in-game social network, with camera and gallery), weather, contacts and the fitness app, which tracks your workout window and Focus. For controls the game never explains (flipping cars, sitting, RydeMe fast travel), see GTA 6 hidden features, and to find missions and shops on the map, see the index guide.

p.h: Explore the map the smart way
l: The Exploration tab. Open the map and check the Exploration tab. BennyCentral says it lists favors for your neighbors and other side activities that are easy to miss. Most of the map starts out under fog, and it only lifts as you travel through each area.

A helicopter to clear the fog. MrRoflWaffles shows a helicopter parked at a spot just south of Hamlet. Fly it around and you clear huge chunks of fog in one go. For him it turns up most reliably in the late afternoon, around 4 to 5 p.m. in-game.

Binoculars before you go in. Before you hit a place full of enemies, BennyCentral suggests pulling out your binoculars and tagging each one from a distance, so you know where everyone is before you make a move.

You can be well armed without spending much. Snipers, a rocket launcher, unique guns and hidden bags of cash are all up for grabs near the start, and the best order to collect them is in GTA 6 secret early items. Before any gunfight, put on body armor: where to buy it, how to equip it and where to find it for free are in how to get body armor in GTA 6.

The cops remember you. They track your car, weapon and outfit. Change clothes fast: hold L1 (LB on Xbox) and press R1 (RB) to take off pieces, like your hat. Keep outfits in your car's trunk to change away from home. More in how to lose the police.

Skip time at your bed. Walk up to your bed at home to skip hours, handy for timed missions or to skip the night. MrDalekJD points out that you get to choose the time you wake up, which beats waiting around.

It's optional: she's your partner in crime either way. If you want to build the relationship, answer her calls, fix up the house (steps, patio fence, balcony, bedroom paint) and bring some cash when you pick her up so you can buy her a beer.
Arekkz Gaming counts five repair jobs around the house, and each one gives the relationship a bump:
patch the bedroom wall;
paint the bedroom (you pick the color once the wall is fixed);
fit new planks on the outside stairs;
fix the roof, reached by the ladder next to the front door;
repair the railing at the back, near the gym equipment.
More in Jason and Lucia's relationship.
At one point in chapter 1, Lucia calls with five optional errands. KultZ went through all of them:
Groceries: carry the bags all the way into the house. Leaving them in the trunk doesn't count.
Flowers in South Key Lento.
A haircut for Jason.
Lucia's necklace at the Siren's Chest store. Budget around $500. He says the gift comes up again later in the story.
Her clothes: pick up the call from an unknown number. A friend of Lucia's has her clothes at the Manatee's Rest bar. Put the bag in the trunk and drive that same car to the prison to pick her up.
KultZ suggests keeping enough cash on you for these errands and stashing the rest.
If you bought the Ultimate Edition, the extras are in the pause menu under Store. Many unlock in chapter 1: car skins show up at any mod shop, and weapon skins in the locker at Ammu-Nation.

Don't forget the car. Arekkz Gaming reminds Ultimate owners about the free upgrade for Jason's car. It unlocks after the car repair mission early in the story: that opens customization, and there you can pick the Ultimate Edition version, which he says comes with better stats and its own paint job. The full list of extras is in how to claim the Ultimate Edition bonuses.
What should you do first in GTA 6? Tweak your settings (run toggle and the map on the View button), push the story until you unlock the tools, and always stash your money at home.
Does your money reset in GTA 6? According to WiLLiSGaming, yes: your cash goes back to zero when chapter 2 starts. Only the family savings, the $5,000 in BuckMe, carries over.
How do you skip time in GTA 6? Go to the bed at your safehouse. You can skip hours and, according to MrDalekJD, pick the time you wake up, for example to wait for a mission or skip the night.
How do you see your missions in GTA 6? On your phone (Up on the D-pad). Messages from characters show suggested jobs and the ones you've done.
Jason's phone: missions, apps and messages all live here.

t: GTA 6 Sunken Treasure: How to Dive Kenton's Shipwrecks and Make Money
r: In GTA 6, dive captain Kenton opens up the shipwrecks with the mission Island Dreams. Dive with the metal detector, collect the treasure and sell it back to him: one dive can pay up to $4,000.

l: Diving shipwrecks is one of the most fun ways to make money early in GTA 6. The jobs come from Kenton, a captain who runs boat trips for divers. You dive with a metal detector, collect the treasure and sell it back to him. GameSpot says the game calls this activity Kenton's Treasures. According to WiLLiSGaming, one dive can pay up to $4,000, and JoblessGarrett did a full round and made $3,200 in under 30 minutes.
Kenton's first job is Island Dreams, in Chapter 1. KultZ says it shows up after the mission Hey Arnold, at Kenton's dive shop on the beach in Key Lento.
That mission teaches you how to dive and hunt for treasure in a wreck. It pays $400, one time only.
In the same mission you get scuba gear and two tools: the Arras Bullhead speargun and the metal detector, according to GameSpot.

Later, Kenton calls you again with more wrecks. He texts you the locations; you collect everything, bring it back and get paid. After a while he offers a fresh batch. KhrazeGaming notes these spots show up on the map with a purple icon and count toward an achievement.

Kenton's shop is marked on the map, and you can take his boat from the dock next to it. If you own another boat, GameSpot says Kenton has the scuba gear, speargun and detector delivered to that boat. RageGamingVideos also got a scuba suit to use on his own boat.
Garrett Lindsay's video shows what diving looks like on PS5:
Going down: the prompt reads DIVE R1, so R1 takes you deeper.
Coming up: the prompt reads SURFACE X, so X brings you back to the surface.
Oxygen: your air bar sits in the top-left corner. Glance at it before you swim into a wreck.
Flashlight: the scuba gear comes with one.
Wildlife: seals swim past in his footage, and he warns that sharks are around too.
He only shows the PS5 version. On Xbox the buttons should sit in the same spots on the pad (RB and A).

Garrett found the gear highlighted in white on a pier while exploring the map, and picked it up with Triangle. The name of the spot isn't clear in the video. His own video description ties the gear to Kenton's diving activities and the mission Island Dreams, so it's most likely the same kit Kenton gives you.

p.h: How to use the metal detector
l: At the wreck, pull out the detector and slowly pan it around until you see a green flash.
Swim that way. The pings speed up and the green light blinks faster as you get closer (GameSpot and KultZ).
At the right spot, a prompt shows up to dig up or grab the treasure.
Check inside the ship too: the chests are usually in there.
Every wreck has several relics and coins. Once you've found them all, that spot counts as done.
Head back to Kenton and sell.
BennyCentral says the detector takes a little getting used to, but once you've got it, wrecks go by fast.

p.h: How many treasures each wreck has
l: NoobBlox found all 7 treasures at Nuestra Señora de la Noche, scattered inside and around the ship, including a purple gemstone and a chest.
In JoblessGarrett's video one wreck had 7 items and another had 5, like a pipe, an antique candlestick, a ceremonial spoon and chests.

BennyCentral showed where each of the 12 treasures sits across two wrecks near Key Lento: 7 in the first and 5 in the second. The counts and items match JoblessGarrett's, and the first wreck, with its purple gemstone and chest, looks like the same Nuestra Señora de la Noche NoobBlox covered.

p.h: All 12 treasures in the two Key Lento wrecks
l: BennyCentral's routine: mark the dive sites on your map, take your boat there (auto drive will steer for you), put on the scuba gear and pull out the metal detector. Its light turns from red to green when you're right on top of a treasure.
First wreck (7 treasures):
Serpentine statue: under the hole, by the big kelp plant.
Candlestick: out in the rubble, near a barrel.
Dragon pipe: next to a fishing net.
Purple gemstone: in the kelp, by a fallen pipe.
Ivory saint: at the bottom of the slope, against the hull.
Pewter gauntlet: in the seagrass, by the timbers.
Buried chest: in a dark rocky area. You have to dig it up. Benny says this is the one everybody misses.
Second wreck (5 treasures):
Golden pendant: in the debris field.
Ceremonial spoon: at the base of a coral.
Chest: tucked under a coral overhang. Pull it out.
Golden chalice: by a block just outside the hole.
Snuff box: in the seagrass, right against the hull wall.
Take everything back to Kenton at his shop in Key Lento. Benny got $2,400 for the whole lot of 12. The name of the first wreck isn't clear in his voiceover.
According to BennyCentral, there are 99 gold doubloons scattered around Leonida, and plenty of them sit on the seabed away from Kenton's wrecks.
Bobcat Key dome houses: the dome-shaped houses on stilts out at sea have doubloons on the seabed underneath them. Dive with the detector and wait for the green light.
Landmarks by the water: those dome houses are a Waink landmark. Benny's tip is that whenever a landmark sits by the water, there's very likely treasure nearby. Scan it, then search with the detector.
Doubloons can be sold at pawn shops too. See collectible cards for how to check collectible values from the map.
GameSpot has found 6 wrecks so far, all in southern Leonida:
Nuestra Señora del Ocho
Nuestra Señora de la Noche
Nuestra Señora de la Etica Laxa
Nuestra Señora Lujuriosa
Urca de Cinco Torres
Urca de Santa Sierra
GameSpot says the list may grow. KhrazeGaming also found plenty of dive spots scattered around the Leonida Keys.
The first mission, Island Dreams, pays $400 (KultZ).
One round of JoblessGarrett's treasure sold for $2,600.
On the way he also found contraband floating at sea and sold it for $1,600 at Brian's lockup.
RageGamingVideos cleared the first wreck marked on the map with just the metal detector and sold the haul for about $1,400, very quickly.

KhrazeGaming says every treasure you bring back is worth $2,400 and every coin $200, with 5 to 7 coins per spot. By his math you'll come back with at least $2,000 per spot. Other channels got less per round, so the payout probably changes from wreck to wreck.
BennyCentral got $2,400 for all 12 treasures from two wrecks combined. That's the same figure KhrazeGaming gives, but for the whole lot rather than per treasure.
According to WiLLiSGaming, the more dives you do, the more Kenton pays and the more locations he sends. Whenever he calls, go.

Sharks. JoblessGarrett got attacked by a tiger shark and nearly died, and BennyCentral and Garrett Lindsay warn about them too. Don't stay in the water longer than you need to. GameSpot says the Arras Bullhead doesn't hold much ammo, but it's your only defense down there. RageGamingVideos killed a shark with it.

The warden. At one wreck, a boat pulled up to warn that searching shipwrecks without a recovery permit is illegal and that finds must be reported. JoblessGarrett ignored it and sold everything anyway.
Stash your cash. If you die or get busted with the money on you, you lose it. See do you lose money when you die.

On the way back, JoblessGarrett found you can switch on the cinematic camera and let your character drive automatically, like in Red Dead Redemption 2. Set a destination, hold Down on the D-pad and press Circle. KhrazeGaming says it works even better on a boat, since there's barely any traffic at sea. More in hidden features.
More ways to make money in how to make money fast in GTA 6.
How do you find sunken treasure in GTA 6? Do Kenton's diving side jobs. He texts you shipwreck locations; dive with the gear he gives you and follow the green flash on the metal detector.
What mission unlocks Kenton's diving in GTA 6? Island Dreams, in Chapter 1. KultZ says it opens up after the mission Hey Arnold, at Kenton's dive shop on the beach in Key Lento.
How much does sunken treasure pay in GTA 6? Up to $4,000 per dive, according to WiLLiSGaming. JoblessGarrett sold one round of treasure for $2,600, and the first mission, Island Dreams, pays $400.
Do you need a permit to dive for treasure in GTA 6? A character warns you that searching shipwrecks without a permit is illegal, but JoblessGarrett ignored it and sold everything with no problem.
Diving a shipwreck with Kenton's scuba gear.

t: How to Get Every GTA 6 Ultimate Edition and Pre-Order Bonus
r: GTA 6's Ultimate Edition and pre-order bonuses unlock bit by bit from Chapter 1 to Chapter 5. Here's where to find each car, weapon, shop and outfit, and which ones are Chapter 1 only.

l: GTA 6's Ultimate Edition and pre-order bonuses don't all show up on day one. Each one unlocks in a specific chapter, from 1 to 5, and sits at a specific spot on the map. Below is when and where to grab every item. The pre-order pack applies to both the Standard and Ultimate Editions; everything else is Ultimate only.
Finish mission 11 in Chapter 1, Coming Home. That unlocks the store in the main menu, where every bonus has an entry telling you which chapter it arrives in and how to collect it.
For the pre-order pack, open the main menu, go to the store and scroll down past GTA+ to the Vintage Vice City Pack.
Almost everything is tracked through the map index. If you haven't used it yet, see how to use the map index.
Both sources mark the Ganado Retro Build, the Dinka Enduro and the Crest Kayak as Chapter 1 only. Neither says what happens if you move on without them, so don't wait.

jayvee, who shows all three in game, says they can only be used during Chapter 1: after that, you can't do anything with them. The bike is tucked in the shadows under Jason's house, and the kayak floats on the ramp next to it. The Retro Build shows up after Joey's mission at Coastal Auto Care, under the pro builds and full kits menu.

The personalized pistols are free to equip.

According to jayvee, Jason's Girardi ES9 unlocks right away: do the mission where you talk to Andrew at the gun store at the start of the game. When it ends, the game tells you your Ultimate Edition content is ready. Go to the store's weapon locker and switch to the variant. He found it stronger and quicker firing than the starting pistol, and you keep it after Chapter 1.
jayvee calls this the best Ultimate Edition bonus so far, and you can hit it in Chapter 1:
The compound is in Southside, Vice City. Drop a pin and call a taxi: it'll take you there as long as you can pay the fare.
As you get close, the game tells you there were gunshots coming from the building, and it shows up on your map as a robbery opportunity.
Security is high. jayvee took out 30 to 40 gang members, and the police joined the shootout.

Behind the counter you'll find the drugs to sell to Brian or Donnie. There's also a unique pistol there: the screen in his video reads Duval Signature ES9 Pistol, although he calls it a K17 out loud and says it has a huge magazine.
Before you leave, check the map: it tells you whether you've grabbed all the valuables.
To get away, he ran off on foot, swapped his hat and sunglasses and, with his car nearby, changed outfits from the trunk to lower his heat.
He says you can come back and hit it again. To sell the drugs, see GTA 6 fence locations. More early rare guns in GTA 6 unique weapons.
Stock 305: according to jayvee, you can't even walk in without the Ultimate Edition.
Sara's Unisex Salon: you can go in during Chapter 1, but the extra haircuts only arrive in Chapters 2 and 4.
One-Eyed Willie's: the shop opens in Chapter 1, but you need an off-road vehicle to use it. jayvee didn't have one yet.
Bonus · What it is · Where to get it
Lucia's pistol · Engraved Klose K17 · Ammu-Nation weapon locker, Variants section
Morgan Revolvers · Morgan variants for Jason and Lucia with palm-tree grips, engravings and a scope · Any Ammu-Nation weapon locker. You don't need to have bought the revolver

'67 Vapid Dominator Buggy and garage · Off-roader plus the Paradise Garage in Watson Bay, which has a weapon locker and a safe spot for stolen goods you plan to fence · Meet Wyman at the motel safehouse and he invites Lucia to the Thrillbilly Mud Club. After a Dirt Track Race, a task appears in the Exploration section of the index

Classic Car Collection · Side activity where you track down and restore abandoned classics for Wyman · Once you have the Dominator, Wyman texts you on WhatUp. Look for Find Cars for Wyman under Exploration
The Vintage Vice City Pack goes to everyone who pre-ordered, on Standard or Ultimate. You can only claim it in Chapter 3:

'55 Vapid Stanier and garage: a task shows up in the Exploration section of the index. The car is parked outside the Ocean View Hotel. Collecting it also unlocks the Bonita Court garage, north of Washington Beach.
80s outfits and hairstyles: once you have the car, the outfits are in your wardrobe and the hairstyles are in the Special section of any salon.
Palm tree weapon pattern, a nod to Tommy Vercetti's shirt: once you have the car, head to any Ammu-Nation and apply it under Cosmetics / Wraps in the weapon's modify menu.
Bonus · What it is · Where to get it
Vice City Style · New outfits, tattoos, hair and beards for Jason and Lucia · Outfits in your wardrobe, tattoos in the Special section of most tattoo parlors, hair and beards at Sara's Unisex Salon

'95 Grotti Cheetah · Red and white 90s sports car with a retro-futuristic livery · Garage under the Pegassi Residences building. An Exploration task in the index helps you find it
To store the new rides, see the garage locations and prices. And since the Paradise Garage can hold stolen goods, the fence locations guide covers where to sell them.

Where are the Ultimate Edition bonuses in GTA 6? Each bonus unlocks in a set chapter at a set spot on the map. The main menu store, which opens after the mission Coming Home, tells you when and where to grab each one.

How do you claim the GTA 6 pre-order bonus? In Chapter 3, a task appears in the Exploration section of the map index. Pick up the '55 Vapid Stanier at the Ocean View Hotel and the outfits, hairstyles and weapon pattern unlock with it.
When do you get the '95 Grotti Cheetah in GTA 6? In Chapter 5. It's parked in the garage under the Pegassi Residences building, and an Exploration task in the map index points you there.
Which Ultimate Edition bonuses are Chapter 1 only? The Ganado Retro Build, the Dinka Enduro motorcycle and the Crest Kayak. Both sources flag all three as Chapter 1 only.
The in-game store lists the Ultimate Edition bonuses, like Jason's vehicles and the Ganado Retro Build.

t: GTA 6 Parachute Location: Where to Buy One, Free Spots and How to Use It
r: In GTA 6 you buy a parachute once at an Ammu-Nation that sells clothes. Free ones wait at all 25 base jump spots, on the Key Lento radio tower, on some skyscraper roofs and on Mount Kalaga.

l: In GTA 6 you only buy a parachute once, at an Ammu-Nation that sells clothing. You can also find free ones at every base jump spot and on top of some buildings. PC Gamer explained where to buy one, GameSpot covered the base jump spots and controls, and Millzaa and Arekkz Gaming grabbed and used the free one on the Key Lento radio tower.
At Ammu-Nation stores that sell clothes. On the map, look for the Ammu-Nation with the shirt icon.
The parachute hangs on a rack inside the store.

p.h: Where to find one for free
l: Base jump spots: according to GameSpot, all 25 base jump spots in the game come with a free parachute. You'll know you've found one by the parachute sitting between two green cones with energy drinks on the ground, and a purple parachute icon shows up on your map. Most are on top of skyscrapers in Vice City, often on the helipad: walk into the lobby and take the elevator up. Typical Gamer found one at the top of a tower with a "PARACHUTE (FULL)" prompt to grab it. The full list is in GTA 6 base jump locations.

Key Lento radio tower: close to Jason's house, right at the start of the game. Climb all the way to the top: the parachute hangs on the railing. Millzaa and Arekkz Gaming both grabbed it. The same climb has a sniper and collectible cards; see GTA 6 secret early items.
Skyscraper roofs: some have a box of parachutes up top.
Mount Kalaga: the tallest peak in Mount Kalaga National Park has a parachute at the top. It's the hard way, but it makes for a nice trip.
Jump out of a plane mid-flight or off a tall building.
In freefall, press the on-screen prompt to pull the chute.
Steer left and right. Lean forward to drop faster or pull back to drop slower.
Jump: near the edge, press Cross (A on Xbox). On a base jump, go off right between the two cones.
Deploy: press Cross (A) again while you're in the air. Millzaa does the same thing, tapping jump a second time to pull the chute.
Brake: hold Cross (A). The canopy pulls up and you lose speed for a moment. You can't hold it forever.
Land: just above the ground, press Triangle (Y) to ditch the chute and drop onto your feet. On a base jump, hitting the ground with the chute still open fails the challenge.
Reset it after use. You only pay once, but after a jump you have to go back to a gun store and pick it off the rack again to add it to your inventory. Or grab one from a rooftop.

The tower chute is single use. Millzaa points out that the parachute on the Key Lento tower only works once: he jumped, opened it, and Jason tossed it away after landing. If you want to keep it, take the ladders back down. Arekkz adds that the tower isn't all that high for a jump, so deploy quickly.
Use it to escape. If the police shoot your plane down, bail out and pull the chute. See the GTA 6 airport.
After the story there's a parachute cheat, unlocked with 50 skydives or base jumps from 300 feet or higher.
Where do you get a parachute in GTA 6? Buy one at an Ammu-Nation that sells clothes, marked with a shirt icon on the map. It hangs on a rack in the store.

Are there free parachutes in GTA 6? Yes. All 25 base jump spots have a free parachute between two green cones. There's another at the top of the Key Lento radio tower near Jason's house, some on skyscraper roofs and one on the tallest peak in Mount Kalaga National Park.

How do you open the parachute in GTA 6? Jump with Cross (A on Xbox) and press it again in the air to deploy. Hold it to slow down for a moment, and press Triangle (Y) just above the ground to ditch the chute and land, according to GameSpot.
Is there a parachute cheat in GTA 6? Yes. It unlocks after 50 skydives or base jumps from 300 feet or higher, after beating the story. The sequence hasn't been published yet.
Mount Kalaga National Park, where a parachute waits on the highest peak, in an official image.
A base jump spot at the top of a tower: two green cones and a free parachute with the PARACHUTE (FULL) prompt.

t: How to Use Auto Drive in GTA 6 (Cars and Boats)
r: In GTA 6, set a destination, hold down on the D-pad while driving and switch to the cinematic camera. Enable Auto Drive then shows up and the car or boat drives itself there.

l: GTA 6 has a built-in auto drive. Set a destination on the map, hold down on the D-pad while you drive and pick the cinematic camera. An Enable Auto Drive prompt then appears: press circle on PS5 (B on Xbox) and your character drives to the marker without you touching the sticks. It works in cars and boats.
JuiceHead on Xbox and Milo on PS5 showed it working first, and SubscribeForTacos and BennyCentral have used it since.
It unlocks early. SubscribeForTacos turned on auto drive on a save that hadn't even finished Chapter 1, so you don't need to push through the story to get it.
Set a destination on the map first. Milo only got it to work with a waypoint already placed.
Get in a car or boat and start driving.
Hold down on the D-pad to open the quick navigation menu, the same one you use to pick GPS targets.
Pick the cinematic camera. The view switches to movie-style angles.
Enable Auto Drive shows up in the bottom corner. Press circle (B on Xbox).
The vehicle now drives itself. Press the same button, now labeled Disable Auto Drive, to take the wheel back. To leave the cinematic camera, the game tells you to hold the D-pad.
For step 5, JuiceHead and Milo press the button once. SubscribeForTacos held circle instead and it worked just as well. BennyCentral simply taps circle (B on Xbox) after holding down on the D-pad.

p.h: The same menu picks your destination
l: Holding down on the D-pad does a second job, BennyCentral explains. It brings up a quick view of what's nearby, missions and shops included, and slows time down while you choose. Pick one and your GPS is set, no big map needed. You can do that and then switch auto drive on straight away.
For more ways to find and mark places, see how the map index works.
While it is on, the corner of the screen shows Speed 1/2/3. On JuiceHead's Xbox, LT and RT move between them; on PS5 that is L2 and R2.
SubscribeForTacos shows speeds 1, 2 and 3 as well, and put it on 3 to sit back for the ride.

Even at the top speed, the car follows traffic laws. It stops at lights and waits its turn, so trips take longer than driving yourself. SubscribeForTacos gives the same warning: you'll be stuck at red lights, so drive yourself if you're in a hurry. JuiceHead's trick is to switch it off, pass the slow car ahead, then switch it back on without stopping.
When you arrive, JuiceHead says the game parks the car in a parking spot for you.

The Gameplay tab in the settings has an Auto Drive option with 2 values. The in-game text says it drives you to your set destination and can only be turned on in the cinematic camera. In JuiceHead's menu it sits on Restricted, which the game describes as available only in safe scenarios. The video never shows the other value. That same tab has more options that make the game easier; see GTA 6 difficulty settings.
There is hardly any traffic on the water, so a boat on auto drive gets there fast. JuiceHead used it all the time to head home: the boat sailed itself right up to the ladder behind Jason's house.

p.h: Cop cars with the siren on
l: In a police car with the siren on, auto drive moves more freely through traffic, though it still sticks to the rules where it can, according to JuiceHead. Milo tested the siren while driving himself: the cars ahead and a group of people in his path moved aside.
For more controls the game never explains, like flipping your car back over and listening to the radio on foot, see GTA 6 hidden features. New to the game? Start with the beginner tips.
How do you turn on auto drive in GTA 6? Set a destination on the map, then hold down on the D-pad while driving. Pick the cinematic camera and press circle (B on Xbox) when Enable Auto Drive appears.
Why can't I use auto drive in GTA 6? It needs a destination set and only works inside the cinematic camera. With the Auto Drive setting on Restricted, it is also limited to safe scenarios.
Does auto drive work on boats in GTA 6? Yes. JuiceHead used it to sail back to Jason's house, and the boat pulled right up to the ladder behind it.
Can you change the auto drive speed in GTA 6? Yes, there are 3 speeds. In JuiceHead's Xbox footage they are on LT and RT, which are L2 and R2 on PS5.
Auto Drive running: the corner shows the 3 speed settings and the Disable Auto Drive prompt.
In the cinematic camera on PS5, the game shows Enable Auto Drive on the circle button.
The Auto Drive setting in the Gameplay tab: on Restricted it only works in safe scenarios.

t: Best GTA 6 Settings to Change Before You Play
r: Set movement speed to Jog, keep aiming on Partial, turn on progress notifications and turn off motion blur. Plus helmet, camera zoom, metric units and phone settings in GTA 6.

l: The best GTA 6 settings to change before you play are Movement Speed (try Jog), Targeting (the default Partial is enough for most people), progress notifications (on), motion blur (off) and the units of measurement if you don't think in miles. This list comes from four English-speaking YouTube channels: NorZZa, BennyCentral, KhrazeGaming and MrDalekJD. The menu names are the ones on screen in NorZZa's video.
Settings sit in the pause menu, split into tabs: Control Scheme, Controller, Gameplay, Display, UI, Camera, Audio and more. Buttons below are PS5. On Xbox, L3 is LS, R2 is RT and square is X.
In the Gameplay tab, under Movement, Movement Speed decides your top speed when the left stick is pushed all the way. There are four options:
Option · Full stick gives you
Walk · A walk. This is the default.
Fast Walk · A quicker walk.
Jog · A jog.
Run · A run.
Sprint still works on top of any of them (click L3, or the button you mapped it to). BennyCentral uses Jog because it gives better control: small stick movements walk, and the edge of the stick jogs.

JorRaptor and JuiceHead go one step further and pick Run. With it, a full push on the stick has you running without touching your stamina. It's not as quick as a real sprint, but you stop having to click the stick all the time. JuiceHead also confirms Walk is the default.
Right below it are two more:
Combat Movement Speed: the same idea, only during fights. It has three options, and NorZZa picks Jog to reach cover and reposition faster.

Stand & Sprint: with it on, pressing sprint while crouched makes you stand up and sprint instead of just moving a bit faster while crouched. It was off in NorZZa's game, and the video suggests turning it on.
At the top of the Gameplay tab, under Combat, Targeting has three modes:
Free Aim: no auto aim at all. Only your own inputs.
Partial: the default. The in-game description says aiming moves toward a nearby target but won't lock on.
Lock-on: the reticle locks onto the target and stays there while you strafe around.
NorZZa thinks Partial is probably enough, and suggests lock-on if you struggle to aim with a controller. Aim Assist Strength, the next line down, lets you fine-tune it.
